to.implementation_strategy: Extend core/backlog.py with a claim-by-id operation exposing claim ownership + lease expiry; add REST endpoint POST /api/v1/backlog/items/{id}/claim (guarded, operator assignment via assignee override). Wire into core/worker.py session start so a worker can claim a specific item; release/expire logic reuses core/release.py lease patterns if present.
dependency_findings: REQUIRES BI-PF-1327 (worktree session model + API-only backlog writes guard) — claim endpoint must obey its write-guard allowlist.
RELATED BI-PF-1325 (PF_API_TOKEN) for auth on the new endpoint.
RELATED BI-PF-1326 (start-from-anywhere wrapper) will call claim-by-id.
conflict_findings: core/backlog.py also touched by BI-PF-1328 (children regeneration) only via config validation — low overlap.
BI-PF-1327's API-only writes guard touches the same REST layer; sequence after 1327 completes.
duplication_findings: No existing claim-by-id API; /api/v1/backlog/groom/approve and /api/v1/backlog/ids:reserve cover adjacent flows but not assignment+lease.
core/backlog_link.py handles item relations, not ownership — no overlap.
to.rationale: Operators need to pin a specific backlog item to a specific worker/session with safe lease semantics; this is the core scheduling primitive for the WG epic.
assumptions: BI-PF-1327's write guard exposes an allowlist that can include claim/checkpoint/delivery endpoints.
Lease model similar to existing worker lease in core/worker.py.
config/engineering-workers.json lists workers that can be assigned.
risks: Lease expiry vs session liveness mismatch could double-assign items.
Write-guard allowlist from BI-PF-1327 not yet defined may force rework of endpoint guard.
Operator assignment could conflict with a worker's in-flight claim — needs takeover policy.
evidence: Candidate components core/backlog.py, core/worker.py, core/release.py exist.
missing_info: Lease duration and renewal cadence for claims.
Takeover policy: can an operator force-reassign an active claim?
